newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks slip after Chicago PMI, home sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks slip after Chicago PMI, home sales.

text.p: Wall Street stocks, which opened higher, declined on Monday after a higher-than-expected reading in the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index for June and a rise in U.S. single-family home sales in May.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell around 51 points or 0.66 percent to 7637, prompting the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading at 1002 EDT/1402 GMT.
Stocks were partly dragged down by a weaker bond market, which dropped 19/32 to a 6.79 percent yield.
The Nasdaq composite shed around three points to 1435.
The Chicagoland Business Barometer rose to a seasonally adjusted 61.5 in June from 56.8 in May, the Purchasing Management Assocation of Chicago said on Monday.
An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy while a reading above 50 suggests expansion.
U.S. single-family home sales rose 7.1 percent in May to a higher-than-forecast 825,000 unit annual rate.

"The data indicates the economy is a little more robust than people thought," Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said. "It is creating nervousness ahead of the FOMC meeting tomorrow."
